name: Peachy Pink
lede: Peachy Pink is a warm, coral-leaning [[pink]] from the xkcd 2010 crowd-name survey, closest in our library to [[salmon|Salmon]].

sections.title: A crowd name, undocumented beyond the survey
sections.body:
The xkcd 2010 survey is the only source our data carries for this exact pairing of words, and who coined it beyond the survey respondents is undocumented [1]. In Munsell terms it sits near 7.0R 7.3/8.9, and the ISCC-NBS lists call its block a "strong yellowish pink" [1].

The nearest standing color in our library is Salmon, about 5.9 units away by CIEDE2000, with [[peach|Peach]] and [[coral|Coral]] close family [1]. The hex is a screen value; no dye or pigment claim follows from the match [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Peachy Pink is one of the rarer matches in our archive, present in 10 of 23,781 paintings by raw coverage and in only 1 by its position in the painting's lightness order, as photographed, rarer than 86% of the named colors we track [2]. Where it does sit within a painting, it plays the midtone, in all 6 of the dated matches counted that way [2].

The earliest match is 1515, in Correggio's *Salvator Mundi* (nga-46167), with later ones running to 1911, 495 years before the name's own 2010 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. That is a resemblance in an aged photograph, not a claim that Correggio mixed this pink or that anyone used this name at the time [2].
